NEW PATIENT VISIT

56 yo man transferring care. Retired from the postal service a couple of years ago after a long career carrying a route. Feels well. No complaints today.

Hx:
- HTN for about 8 years, on HCTZ 25 mg every morning. Home cuff readings he remembers are mostly in the 130s.
- High cholesterol, on atorvastatin 20 mg for several years. No muscle aches.
- Takes a baby aspirin daily; started on his own years ago because of his father's heart history.
No surgeries.

Meds: HCTZ 25 mg qAM, atorvastatin 20 mg qHS, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.

FHx: father had coronary disease young, around 52. Mother with high blood pressure. Brother on cholesterol medicine. A paternal uncle had gout.
SHx: married, lives in Easthampton. Never smoked. A beer or a glass of wine once or twice a week. Walks most mornings.

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, edema, headaches or vision change. No joint complaints.

Exam: well appearing. Ht 178 cm. BP slightly above goal, see flowsheet. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no bruit. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Ext without edema, pulses 2+. Skin no rashes.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. Hypertension - near goal on HCTZ. Continue. Recheck with labs.
2. Hyperlipidemia - continue atorvastatin 20. Fasting lipids today.
3. Health maintenance - colonoscopy per him about 3 years ago, normal; requesting old records to confirm. HCV and HIV screens today, he agrees. Flu shot given.
CMP, CBC, lipids drawn. F/u in about 6 months, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: lumps on elbows and knees

58M here because of hard bumps over both elbows and the fronts of both knees that he first noticed over the past couple of months. A couple of them have leaked a white, gritty material. Not very painful.
On direct questioning: for something like ten years he has had spells of a hot, red, very sore big toe (either side), sometimes so tender a sheet hurts. Each one goes away by itself in a few days, so he never brought it up. Last one was before Christmas. Uncle had gout.
Meds: HCTZ 25, atorvastatin 20, ASA 81. NKDA.

Exam: firm subcutaneous nodules over both olecranon areas and both prepatellar areas, a few with reddened skin over them, one on the R elbow with a little chalky discharge. No warmth or effusion in knees. Feet: no active inflammation of 1st MTPs today.

A/P
Nodules + episodic podagra - picture is gout with tophi until proven otherwise. He is on a thiazide.
- Referred to rheumatology for evaluation and long-term management; they can aspirate/confirm and start therapy.
- Keep the draining spot clean and covered.
- For a flare before then, call; we would treat it.

documents.title: Rheumatology Consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE RHEUMATOLOGY - CONSULTATION LETTER
Date of visit: 02/28/2023
Re: Rodney Jacobs, DOB 09/09/1964
Referred by: primary care

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Jacobs, a 58-year-old retired postal carrier.

History: He describes roughly a decade of intermittent attacks in the great toes - intense pain with redness and swelling, each settling over several days without any treatment. More recently he has developed firm lumps over the olecranon and prepatellar bursae.
PMH: hypertension, hyperlipidemia.
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, aspirin 81 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: paternal uncle with gout; father with early coronary disease; mother hypertensive; brother with hyperlipidemia.
Social: retired postal worker, never smoker, alcohol 1-2 drinks per week.

Examination: Multiple subcutaneous nodules over both elbows and both knees, firm, with erythema of the overlying skin; several are draining chalky white material. No acute synovitis today.

Laboratory: serum uric acid 9.5 mg/dL (reference 3.5-7.2).

Impression: Chronic tophaceous gout.

Recommendations:
1. Allopurinol 100 mg daily, to be increased by our office every few weeks toward a serum urate below 6.
2. Colchicine 0.6 mg daily for flare prophylaxis for the first 6 months.
3. Hydrochlorothiazide raises urate; we would ask that primary care substitute another antihypertensive.
4. We will follow his urate and titrate.

Sincerely,
Outpatient Rheumatology

documents.title: Saw the heart doctor yesterday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi Doc, just so you know I went back to cardiology yesterday. I finally started the new heart pill (isosorbide) a week ago. My walks are better, the chest pressure on the hill is mostly gone. But I get dizzy if I jump up out of the chair too fast. They said my pressure was 102 over 70 and pulse 94 in the office. They said to get up slow and keep taking it. Should I be worried about the low pressure with my lisinopril? Rodney

documents.title: Re: Saw the heart doctor yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know. The nitrate pill commonly does that in the first weeks. Keep taking it as cardiology said, stand up in stages, and drink enough fluids. If you get close to fainting or actually pass out, call us right away. Let's have you come in in two weeks so we can check your pressure sitting and standing.

reports.text: Noncontrast CT of the head. Hypodense area in the left frontal lobe. No intracranial hemorrhage. No mass effect or midline shift. Ventricles normal in size. Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoids clear.
reports.conclusion: Left frontal lobe hypodensity, consistent with ischemic infarct. No hemorrhage.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - CLINICAL SUMMARY (fax)
DOS 07/01/2026
Jacobs, Rodney, 61 M, DOB 09/09/1964
Brought in by wife: she noticed he suddenly could not get his words out and was not using his right arm normally.
PMH: CAD with stable angina, MI about one year ago (06/2025), HTN, HLD, chronic tophaceous gout.
Meds: aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, isosorbide dinitrate 20 mg BID, lisinopril, allopurinol.
Allergies: NKDA. Never smoker; alcohol 1-2 drinks/week.
Exam: awake and alert, visibly frustrated. Speech halting and nonfluent, short phrases. Comprehension intact, follows commands; repetition impaired. Weakness of R face and R arm. Unable to perform coordinated R hand movements on command though moves the hand spontaneously.
CT head: hypodensity L frontal lobe; no hemorrhage.
Impression: acute ischemic stroke, left MCA territory.
Disposition: admitted to the stroke service.

documents.title: Wife calling - patient hospitalized
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife Darlene called. Rodney was admitted yesterday with a stroke - trouble talking and a weak right arm. He is on the stroke unit, more alert this morning. She wanted us to know and asked what to do about his pills at home; told her the hospital will manage meds while he's in and to bring the discharge paperwork to his follow-up. Routed to PCP. Will book post-discharge visit once he is home.

medications.reason: increase to high-intensity statin after stroke

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit - Stroke
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
POST-HOSPITAL VISIT
Here with his wife. ED summary received 7/7: 7/1 sudden nonfluent speech and R face/arm weakness, CT with L frontal hypodensity, admitted with L MCA territory ischemic stroke. Discharge summary not yet received; requested.
Per wife and patient: about five days in the hospital. Home since. Speech coming back - he gets words out in short sentences and gets stuck on some; understands everything. R hand clumsy, grip weaker. Doing outpatient speech therapy twice a week and occupational therapy for the hand, set up by the hospital. Neurology clinic follow-up booked for September. Not driving; wife drives. No new chest pain. Hospital did not change his pills per the bottles he brought.
Meds (bottles reviewed): lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 20, aspirin 81, isosorbide dinitrate 20 BID, allopurinol 300. NKDA.

Exam: alert, cooperative. Speech nonfluent with word-finding pauses, comprehension intact, repetition still effortful. Mild R lower facial weakness. R grip 4/5, R arm drift absent; L side normal. Gait steady without device. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
1. Ischemic stroke, L MCA territory (07/2026) with residual nonfluent speech and R hand weakness - improving. Continue speech and OT. Keep neurology follow-up. Not to drive until neurology says so.
2. Atherosclerotic disease (CAD with prior MI, now stroke) - increase atorvastatin to 80 mg nightly. CMP and lipids today as baseline; repeat lipids/LFTs in about 8 weeks. Continue aspirin.
3. HTN - at goal today, continue lisinopril.
4. Gout - quiet on allopurinol.
Return 9/29, sooner if needed. Spent 45 min, more than half counseling patient and wife.

documents.title: Labs from last week
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Rodney and Darlene - the blood work from Friday is back. Kidney and liver tests are normal, which is the baseline we wanted before the higher atorvastatin dose. Cholesterol numbers reflect the old dose; we'll recheck on the new dose at your September visit. Keep up with the therapy.

documents.title: Outpatient therapy plan of care
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Received by fax from outpatient rehabilitation: speech-language pathology and occupational therapy plans of care for Rodney Jacobs, both requesting physician signature. Diagnosis on the forms: left MCA ischemic stroke. Frequency 2x/week for 8 weeks each. Placed in PCP signature folder.
